full_text_en:
Tengzhou City Suburb Credit Cooperative v. China Construction Bank, Zaozhuang City Xuecheng District Sub-branch — Dispute over Negotiable Instrument

[Ruling Summary]

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 76 of the Guaranty Law, where a party uses a bank draft as a pledge certificate and separately establishes a pledge right over such draft in writing, and the issuing bank confirms the same, the pledge of the draft shall be recognized as valid.

Plaintiff: Tengzhou City Suburb Credit Cooperative. Domicile: Shanguo North Road, Tengzhou City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Yuan Kehong, Director of the said Credit Cooperative.

Defendant: China Construction Bank, Zaozhuang City Xuecheng District Sub-branch. Domicile: Yongfu North Road, Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province.

Person in Charge: Zhu Huihua, Branch Manager.

The Plaintiff, Tengzhou City Suburb Credit Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as "Suburb Credit Cooperative"), filed an action with the Intermediate People's Court of Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province, against the Defendant, China Construction Bank, Zaozhuang City Xuecheng District Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as "Xuecheng CCB"), concerning a dispute over a negotiable instrument.

Plaintiff's Allegations: Tengzhou Jinlilai Coal Washing Plant (hereinafter referred to as "Coal Washing Plant"), using a bank draft of RMB 750,000 issued by the Taozhuang Office affiliated with the Defendant as a pledge certificate, borrowed RMB 750,000 from the Plaintiff. Upon maturity of the loan, the Coal Washing Plant failed to repay. When the Plaintiff deposited the pledged bank draft with the Tengzhou People's Bank for clearing, the Defendant refused to perform its payment obligation, resulting in the Plaintiff's loan of RMB 750,000 remaining unrecovered. The Plaintiff requested the court to order the Defendant to pay the draft amount of RMB 750,000 plus corresponding interest.

Defendant's Defense: The bank draft on which the Plaintiff bases its claim was illegally issued by Qu Jidong, former Deputy Director of the Defendant's Taozhuang Office, without the Coal Washing Plant having paid any consideration for it. According to the illegally issued instrument, the holder should be the Coal Washing Plant, not the Plaintiff. The Plaintiff does not enjoy any rights under the instrument and is not entitled to claim payment from the Defendant.

The Intermediate People's Court of Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province, found the following facts upon trial:

In May 1997, Zhang Zongqian, a business representative of the Coal Washing Plant, requested Qu Jidong, Deputy Director of the Defendant's Taozhuang Office, to provide a loan guarantee for him and promised to give a kickback. On May 28, 1997, Qu Jidong, taking advantage of his position as Deputy Director of the Taozhuang Office, issued a bank draft numbered VIV00316605 (hereinafter referred to as "Draft No. 5") without receiving any funds. The next day, he received an IOU from Liu Baoting, the legal representative of the Coal Washing Plant, and business representative Zhang Zongqian, stating: "Borrowed one bank draft of RMB 750,000 from Taozhuang Office, Xuecheng CCB. Borrowers: Liu Baoting, Zhang Zongqian," and affixed with the financial seal of the Coal Washing Plant. The bank draft recorded the drawer as the Taozhuang Office, the payee as the Coal Washing Plant, and the amount as RMB 750,000. On the same day, the Coal Washing Plant and the Plaintiff, Suburb Credit Cooperative, entered into a pledge loan contract stipulating that the Coal Washing Plant would borrow RMB 750,000 from the Suburb Credit Cooperative for a term of one month, with the subject matter of the pledge being a "draft." Upon execution of the contract, the Coal Washing Plant delivered Draft No. 5 and a "Declaration of Pledge of Rights in Kind" to the Suburb Credit Cooperative. The declaration bore the seals of the issuing bank, Taozhuang Office, and the payee, Coal Washing Plant, and its main content stated that the Coal Washing Plant used Draft No. 5 owned by it as a pledge certificate for the right to borrow from the Suburb Credit Cooperative. The Suburb Credit Cooperative accordingly extended a loan of RMB 750,000 to the Coal Washing Plant. On June 26, 1997, just before the loan was due, Qu Jidong, fearing that if the Coal Washing Plant could not repay on time and the Suburb Credit Cooperative exercised its pledge right, the fact of his illegal issuance of the bank draft would be exposed, issued another bank draft numbered VIV00316608 (hereinafter referred to as "Draft No. 8") without receiving any funds. The Coal Washing Plant used Draft No. 8 to exchange Draft No. 5 from the Suburb Credit Cooperative and simultaneously delivered to the Suburb Credit Cooperative a "Declaration of Pledge of Rights in Kind" specifying the pledge certificate as Draft No. 8. Draft No. 8 also recorded the drawer as the Taozhuang Office, the payee as the Coal Washing Plant, the amount as RMB 750,000, and the date of issue as June 26, 1997. The endorser column of the draft bore the financial seal of the Coal Washing Plant and the seal of its legal representative, Liu Baoting, but the endorsee column was left blank. In the "Signature and Seal of Holder for Presentment for Payment to the Bank" column of the draft, the "Financial Seal of Tengzhou Jinlilai Coal Washing Plant" and the seal of legal representative "Liu Baoting" were affixed, and the words "Entrust Suburb Credit Cooperative for Collection" were written. After the loan matured, the Coal Washing Plant failed to repay. On July 17, 1997, the Suburb Credit Cooperative submitted Draft No. 8 to the Tengzhou People's Bank for collection of RMB 750,000 from Xuecheng CCB through the clearing system. Upon sight of the draft, Xuecheng CCB notified the Taozhuang Office to process the payment. Qu Jidong, the former Deputy Director of the Taozhuang Office, after receiving the draft, absconded with it. Xuecheng CCB then reported the case to the procuratorial authorities and refused to pay the draft amount to the Suburb Credit Cooperative. Three days after absconding, Qu Jidong sent the draft back to Xuecheng CCB, which then returned the draft to the Suburb Credit Cooperative but still refused payment. During the trial of this case, Xuecheng CCB issued a notice of dishonor to the Suburb Credit Cooperative, specifying the reasons for dishonor as: first, the Coal Washing Plant had acquired the instrument in bad faith; and second, the actual settlement amount of the instrument was not written in duplicate.

It was further found that the case of Qu Jidong illegally issuing financial instruments had already been adjudicated by the Xuecheng District People's Court of Zaozhuang City.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including Draft No. 5 and Draft No. 8, the loan contract, the "Declaration of Pledge of Rights in Kind," the notice of dishonor, the Criminal Judgment No. (2001) Xue Xing Chu Zi No. 63 of the Xuecheng District People's Court, and the statements of both parties. The evidence has been subjected to cross-examination and authentication and may serve as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

The Intermediate People's Court of Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province, held:

Article 76 of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Guaranty Law") provides: "Where a pledge is made by using drafts, checks, promissory notes, bonds, certificates of deposit, warehouse receipts, or bills of lading, the document of title shall be delivered to the pledgee within the time limit agreed upon in the contract. The pledge contract shall become effective upon the delivery of the document of title." In this case, Draft No. 8, on which the Plaintiff Suburb Credit Cooperative bases its claim, was issued by the Taozhuang Office affiliated with the Defendant Xuecheng CCB. The bank draft contains all necessary particulars and is clear and definite in content; it is a valid bank draft. The Coal Washing Plant, as the holder of the bank draft, entered into a pledge loan contract with the Suburb Credit Cooperative using Draft No. 5 as a pledge certificate for the right; this contract represented the true intent of both parties. The contract is clear in content and lawful; the draft has been delivered; therefore, the pledge loan contract is a valid contract. Shortly before the loan matured, when the Coal Washing Plant used Draft No. 8 to exchange Draft No. 5, it delivered to the Suburb Credit Cooperative a declaration specifying the pledge certificate for the right as Draft No. 8. Therefore, the Coal Washing Plant's intention to continue using Draft No. 8 as a pledge certificate for the right was genuine, and the pledge right established with Draft No. 8 remained valid.

Paragraph 1 of Article 37 of the "Measures for the Settlement of Payments" provides: "Presentment for payment through the collecting bank or through the clearing system to the payer or the agent payer shall be deemed as presentment for payment by the holder; the date of such presentment for payment shall be the date on which the holder submits the instrument to its开户行." Paragraph 2 provides: "The payer or the agent payer shall make full payment on the day of sight of the instrument." In this case, the Suburb Credit Cooperative, as the opening bank of the holder Coal Washing Plant, has the right to collect the draft amount from the issuing bank Xuecheng CCB when the Coal Washing Plant entrusts it to collect the proceeds of Draft No. 8. Furthermore, because the pledge relationship between the Suburb Credit Cooperative and the Coal Washing Plant concerning Draft No. 8 was validly established, the Suburb Credit Cooperative enjoys a pledge right over the proceeds of the draft presented for payment by the Coal Washing Plant, meaning that the proceeds collected from Draft No. 8 should be used to satisfy the Coal Washing Plant's debt in priority. Therefore, the Suburb Credit Cooperative is entitled to demand payment of the draft amount from Xuecheng CCB. Xuecheng CCB, as the drawer of the draft and the payer, has the obligation to pay unconditionally upon sight. The Suburb Credit Cooperative's claims are lawful and are supported by this court. The defenses raised by Xuecheng CCB are untenable and are not accepted.

Accordingly, the Intermediate People's Court of Zaozhuang City, Shandong Province, rendered its judgment on April 2, 2002:

The Defendant shall pay to the Plaintiff the draft amount of RMB 750,000 plus corresponding interest (the interest shall be calculated according to the同期 loan interest rate published by the People's Bank of China from July 17, 1997 until the date of entry of this judgment) within ten days after this judgment takes effect.

After the judgment was pronounced, Xuecheng CCB appealed to the High People's Court of Shandong Province. Its grounds for appeal were: (1) In the "Signature and Seal of Holder for Presentment for Payment to the Bank" column on the back of Draft No. 8, the financial seal of the Coal Washing Plant and the seal of its legal representative had been affixed, and the words "Entrust Suburb Credit Cooperative for Collection" were written. Therefore, Draft No. 8 had been used by the holder Coal Washing Plant for entrustment for collection and could objectively no longer be used for pledge. (2) Pursuant to Paragraph 2 of Article 35 of the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Negotiable Instruments Law"), Article 29 of the "Measures for the Settlement of Payments," and Article 55 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Negotiable Instruments," a pledge of a negotiable instrument is a formal act; a pledge endorsement must be made on the instrument itself, otherwise no instrument pledge is constituted. On the issue of whether an instrument pledge relationship is established, the Negotiable Instruments Law, as a special law relative to the Guaranty Law, should prevail over the Guaranty Law under the principle that special law prevails over general law. In determining the requirements for establishing a pledge of a draft in this case, the Negotiable Instruments Law and relevant judicial interpretations should apply in priority. The trial court's judgment, which found that the Suburb Credit Cooperative enjoyed a pledge right on the draft based on the Guaranty Law, was erroneous. (3) The trial court held that "the proceeds collected from Draft No. 8 should be used to satisfy the Coal Washing Plant's debt in priority." Since the trial court recognized the Coal Washing Plant as the holder of the instrument right and the Suburb Credit Cooperative only as having priority over the proceeds, the Coal Washing Plant should first exercise its instrument right to obtain the proceeds before the Suburb Credit Cooperative could exercise its priority right. If the appellant refused to pay, only the Coal Washing Plant could claim the draft amount. The trial court's holding that the Suburb Credit Cooperative's priority over the Coal Washing Plant's draft proceeds was transformed into a right to claim payment from the appellant lacked a legal basis. In summary, the Coal Washing Plant and the Suburb Credit Cooperative did not establish a valid pledge relationship over Draft No. 8. The Suburb Credit Cooperative is not the holder of Draft No. 8 and does not enjoy any rights under it; it is not entitled to demand payment from the appellant. The trial court's dismissal of the appellant's claims was erroneous and should be reversed.

The appellee, Suburb Credit Cooperative, argued in response: (1) Although the Negotiable Instruments Law stipulates that a pledge of a draft shall be endorsed with the notation "pledge," it does not negate the validity of pledging a draft by other means. The trial court's finding that the instrument pledge was valid was correct. (2) The Taozhuang Office affiliated with the appellant twice issued bank drafts to the Coal Washing Plant and twice signed and sealed the "Declaration of Pledge of Rights in Kind." Therefore, the appellant was not only aware of but also actively acknowledged the use of Draft No. 8 as a pledge certificate for the right. This confirmed both the authenticity and validity of Draft No. 8 and recognized the use of this draft as a pledge guarantee for the Coal Washing Plant's loan from the appellee, constituting a promise to the pledgee to realize the pledge right. When the Coal Washing Plant failed to perform its obligation, the appellee was entitled to exercise its instrument right to realize the pledge. The Coal Washing Plant, as the payee of Draft No. 8, had an absolute right to settlement of the draft against the appellant. The appellant had an obligation to pay upon sight and could not set up defenses against the appellee's instrument right based on defenses it had against the Coal Washing Plant. The trial court's judgment was correct and should be affirmed.

Upon trial, the High People's Court of Shandong Province, in addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, further found:

The Taozhuang Office affiliated with Xuecheng CCB and the Coal Washing Plant both affixed their seals to the "Declaration of Pledge of Rights in Kind" dated June 26, 1997. The declaration stated: "I (the pledgor) have ownership of the following securities: Tengzhou Jinlilai Coal Washing Plant, draft amount RMB 750,000, VIV00316608, and have now obtained a secured loan by way of pledge from the Suburb Credit Cooperative (name of lending cooperative). Borrower: Tengzhou Jinlilai Coal Washing Plant, loan amount: RMB 750,000, term: from June 26, 1997 to July 25, 1997. From this date, please stop any report of loss of the above-mentioned instruments. After the loan is repaid, please make payment upon endorsement of the lending cooperative. If the borrower fails to repay the loan at maturity, the lending cooperative may, by virtue of the pledge agreement, the notice calling in the loan, and this declaration, withdraw the principal and interest (or go through the transfer procedures). Please confirm."

The High People's Court of Shandong Province held that the focus of the dispute between the parties was: whether a valid pledge relationship was established between the Suburb Credit Cooperative and the Coal Washing Plant over Draft No. 8, and whether Xuecheng CCB should pay the draft amount to the Suburb Credit Cooperative.

The Coal Washing Plant made both an endorsement for entrustment for collection on the back of Draft No. 8 and set up a pledge on the same draft. Since it was the holder of the instrument, after making the endorsement for entrustment for collection on the instrument, it had the right, prior to the completion of the entrusted collection, to cancel the entrustment and further dispose of the draft by way of pledge. Therefore, the appellant's ground of appeal that a draft could no longer be pledged after an endorsement for entrustment for collection was untenable.

Regarding whether a valid pledge relationship was established between the Suburb Credit Cooperative and the Coal Washing Plant, not only the Negotiable Instruments Law and the Guaranty Law but also the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China" and the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Negotiable Instruments" should apply. Paragraph 2 of Article 35 of the Negotiable Instruments Law provides that when a draft is pledged, the notation "pledge" shall be recorded on the endorsement. However, it does not provide that if the notation "pledge" is not recorded, the pledge is not effective or is void. Article 76 of the Guaranty Law provides: "Where a pledge is made by using drafts, checks, promissory notes, bonds, certificates of deposit, warehouse receipts, or bills of lading, the document of title shall be delivered to the pledgee within the time limit agreed upon in the contract. The pledge contract shall become effective upon the delivery of the document of title." Therefore, endorsement for pledge is not the exclusive method of creating a pledge on an instrument; concluding a pledge contract and delivering the instrument can also create such a pledge. Paragraph 1 of Article 31 of the Negotiable Instruments Law provides: "For a draft transferred by endorsement, the endorsements shall be continuous. The holder shall prove its right to the draft by the continuity of endorsements; for a draft obtained by other lawful means without endorsement by endorsement, the holder shall prove its right to the draft by providing evidence according to law." For a pledge of an instrument, the pledge endorsement is direct evidence that the instrument holder enjoys a pledge right on the instrument. If there is no pledge endorsement, a written pledge contract constitutes lawful evidence for the instrument holder to prove that it enjoys the pledge right on the instrument. Where the instrument holder holds the instrument and has a written pledge contract, it shall be determined that the holder enjoys the pledge right on the instrument. Article 98 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "Where a draft, check, or promissory note is used as pledge, and the pledgor and the pledgee have not recorded the notation 'pledge' on the endorsement, if the pledge is set up against a bona fide third party, the people's court shall not support it." Accordingly, the recording of the notation "pledge" on the endorsement is not a requirement for the acquisition of the pledge right on the instrument; it is merely a requirement for the pledge to be effective against third parties. Although Article 55 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Negotiable Instruments" provides that "where a pledge is made on a draft in accordance with Paragraph 2 of Article 35 of the Negotiable Instruments Law... or where the pledgor, without recording the notation 'pledge' on the draft or an allonge, separately concludes a pledge contract or pledge clause, no instrument pledge is constituted," because this provision was promulgated earlier than the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China," the provisions of the latter Interpretation shall apply to this case. In summary, in this case, a pledge contract was concluded between the Suburb Credit Cooperative and the Coal Washing Plant, and the Coal Washing Plant delivered the bank draft into the possession of the Suburb Credit Cooperative. Thus, a valid instrument pledge relationship was established on Draft No. 8, and the Suburb Credit Cooperative acquired the pledge right on the instrument.

The Coal Washing Plant obtained the bank draft without paying consideration. As the drawer, Xuecheng CCB could set up defenses against the Coal Washing Plant. The pledge right on the instrument acquired by the Suburb Credit Cooperative through concluding a pledge contract and delivering the instrument of title should, in principle, succeed to the defects in the instrument right of the pledgor, the Coal Washing Plant. Therefore, Xuecheng CCB could have exercised its right of defense against the Suburb Credit Cooperative. However, because the Taozhuang Office affixed its seal on the "Declaration of Pledge of Rights in Kind," which contained the statement: "If the borrower fails to repay the loan at maturity, the lending cooperative may, by virtue of the pledge agreement, the notice calling in the loan, and this declaration, withdraw the principal and interest," such affixing of its seal indicated that it had expressly waived its right of defense, constituting a promise to the Suburb Credit Cooperative to realize the pledge right. Consequently, when the Suburb Credit Cooperative exercised its pledge right against Xuecheng CCB, the latter should pay the principal and interest of the draft amount in accordance with its promise. The appellant's ground of appeal that the Suburb Credit Cooperative was not entitled to demand payment from it was untenable.

In conclusion, the grounds of appeal raised by Xuecheng CCB were untenable and were not supported. The trial court's judgment was correct and should be affirmed. Accordingly, the High People's Court of Shandong Province, pursuant to Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (1) of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered its judgment on June 18, 2002:

Appeal dismissed; judgment affirmed.

This judgment is final.
